verdict.reason: Three of the seven blockers are not closed by their mechanism (QE-R7A-01, QE-R7A-02, QE-R7A-05). Five material equivalent paths were found (QE-R7A1-01 to 05, two HIGH): a re-applied move keeps the equipment of its history; the weekly review's next-week start is re-derived without its systemic hold and confirmed loads; a return correction across the week boundary does not supersede; same-day eligibility differs between the adaptation handlers and the rest; the merge still loses a known load behind an unreadable one. Each has a minimal reproduction and a required change for the single correction cycle.

blockers.evidence: Return re-base survives an equipment change in both orders (rerun qe-recheck-P1 S1: returnStrengthErasedByEquipmentChange false, sameEitherOrder true). The mechanism the task contract names (next week's start set by a decision of this week is re-derived) remains through C3's evidence branch: the weekly review's systemic hold and its confirmed-load adoption are re-derived differently by an equipment, schedule or goal change the same evening (QE-R7A1-02; qe-a1-P04, qe-a1-P10).

Short return now eases the same-day quality at 05:00 and 21:00 (rerun qe-recheck-P2: sameRunsEitherClock true). Its mechanism (date > asOfLocal instead of aheadOf) remains in fatigueSessions, unavailableSessions, conflictSessions and the move-slot filter (r6-composition.mjs:52, 64, 72, 96) against C1's 'one definition for every handler' (QE-R7A1-04; qe-a1-P06).

One race after return then postponement in either order (rerun qe-recheck-P1 S2). Oracle O6 (one live race on the current event date): 0 violations in 5,000 random sequences (qe-a1-P09 both seeds). Author grids: each event-date order equals its later statement alone.

Null-load case fixed (rerun qe-recheck-P4 4a mergedEqualsUnion true; P5 5a loadsBehindUnion []). A present but unreadable load (no unit, 'LBS', 'pounds') in the chosen entry still makes the other report's 80 kg unknown in either arrival order, because filled() and the readers use two definitions of known (QE-R7A1-05; qe-a1-P07).

HOLD keeps the repetition target 5 for lighter shortfalls at 77.5 and 75 kg; ADVANCE at a lighter load takes the logged repetitions (rerun qe-recheck-P3). Engineering only; the dose reading is the SSCTR's.

Fatigue or an unavailable day, then an event change: same either order, adaptation kept (rerun qe-recheck-P1 S3). Mutant 'a missed-session move is never re-applied' is caught (qe-a1-P11). A new defect inside the re-application of moves is reported separately as QE-R7A1-01 (the adaptation is no longer lost; it is rebuilt with history content).

Engineering side: author D56 grid passes (verifier). qe-a1-P08: on rows actually written by the R6-closure runtime (300 legacy rows read by FREEZE-A1, 24 timelines), 0 cap rises or ends after a trimmed week and 0 capped jumps above the largest executed count plus one. Formulation is the SSCTR's.
Engineering side only, as part of the D56 family above; no equivalent restoration jump found in any representation I ran. Closure also needs the SSCTR's acceptance of the semantics (Founder §10).

newFindings.class: C4 x C2: an adaptation re-applied under a newer context (moved content not composed for the slot date)
newFindings.mechanism: reapply MISSED_SESSION (r6-composition.mjs:111-117) re-runs missedMove; moveCandidates (:54) places clone(target), the missed session's history prescription, into the slot without composing it for the slot date's context (templatesForDate / substitution). equipmentChange (r6-adaptation.mjs:536-543) then finds no swap in the window case and answers KEEP ('Planned exercises already fit the available equipment'). C7 has no per-date equipment check. The missed-session handler itself does the same when the slot lies in an equipment window stated earlier (pre-existing on FREEZE-2).
newFindings.reproduction: qe-a1-P01-moved-content-after-equipment.mjs: strengthDays [0,2,5], runDays [1,3,6]; weeks 0-2 executed; week 3 Tuesday 07:00 MISSED_SESSION w3-str-d0 (MOVE to w3-str-d2), Tuesday 07:30 EQUIPMENT_CHANGE ['DUMBBELLS','BENCH'] -> w3-str-d2 prescribes back-squat 2x5 KNOWN 82.5 (BARBELL, RACK); the window variant answers KEEP/KEEP with the same row; reverse order gives goblet-squat 2x5 ESTABLISH. qe-a1-P01b and qe-a1-P09 (seed 1013, O2): a window stated before, then the Monday miss, moves the barbell squat into the window.
newFindings.requiredChange: Compose a moved session's content for the slot's date under the context in force there (the same substitution an equipment change applies), or do not offer / consume the move when its content is unavailable on that date; add per-date equipment availability to C7 (fail closed); tests for move x equipment change in both orders (permanent and window) and for a move into a window stated before.

newFindings.class: C3 'one rule': the next-week start set by the weekly review is re-derived without the review's inputs (QE-R7A-01 mechanism through the evidence branch)
newFindings.mechanism: weeklyReview (r6-adaptation.mjs:339) gates with systemic (SYSTEMIC_SIGNAL recorded on the week, or ev.systemicConvergence) and with this review's loadConfirmations. evidenceStart (:237-240, evidenceRule in composeWeeks for equipment and return changes once the week is complete) and rebuild (:444, schedule, goal and learned-arrangement changes) compute weeklyGates without systemic, and loggedLoads(ctx.ev, ctx.confirmations) reads only the current review's confirmations, which are not stored.
newFindings.reproduction: A (qe-a1-P04): runDays [1,4,6], strengthDays [0,2]; weeks 0-2 executed; week 3 Sunday 07:00 SYSTEMIC_FATIGUE (nothing left to reduce, SYSTEMIC_SIGNAL), Sunday 21:00 weekly review with every report (all gates HOLD, week 4 at 3 sets), Sunday 22:00 SCHEDULE_CHANGE {runDays:[1,3,6]} or GOAL_CHANGE {strength:HYPERTROPHY} -> all 10 gates ADVANCE and 7 exercises 3 -> 4 sets in week 4; EQUIPMENT_CHANGE ['DUMBBELLS','BENCH'] (permanent, or a window over next Monday) -> 6 exercises 3 -> 4 sets. qe-a1-P05: the weekly review's learned-rearrangement branch advances EASY and LONG under convergence (gate difference only in that profile). B (qe-a1-P10): runDays [1,3,6], strengthDays [2,5]; week-0 weekly review with loadConfirmations 20 kg for db-calf-raise, db-rdl and db-split-squat (KNOWN 20); an equipment swap, schedule or goal change at 22:00 sets them back to FROM_LOG pendingLoad 20 (week 1: 2x7 FROM_LOG instead of 2x6 KNOWN 20).
newFindings.requiredChange: Once the weekly review of a complete week has set next week's start, a later change of that week keeps it (as for a return's re-base), or re-derives it with exactly the review's inputs (the systemic determination and the confirmations, recorded on the week); one function for weeklyReview, evidenceStart and rebuild; tests: the held start and the confirmed loads survive an equipment, schedule and goal change after the review.

newFindings.class: C5 return supersession across the week boundary (the author's '16-day return corrected to 5 days' path)
newFindings.mechanism: returnAfterPause (r6-adaptation.mjs:614) reads startBeforeReturn only when pauseWeek === w; otherwise it reads program.stateTrace[pauseWeek], which an earlier return that re-planned that week has overwritten with its re-entry start.
newFindings.reproduction: qe-a1-P02-return-correction-next-week.mjs: runDays [1,3,6], strengthDays [2,5]; weeks 0-4 executed; week 5 Monday-Thursday not trained; Friday 21:00 return 16 days (re-entry from Saturday); Sunday 21:00 weekly review (Saturday and Sunday reported); correction 'break was Monday-Thursday of week 5, 4 days'. At Sunday 22:00 -> week 6 pre-break doses (back-squat 4x5 @85, runs 48/45/75). At Monday 07:00 of week 6 -> re-entry step 0 (1x5 @RIR4, runs 15/15/20; db-rdl and db-split-squat reset from step 1 to 0). FREEZE-2 gives the re-entry at both clocks.
newFindings.requiredChange: Read program.weeks[pauseWeek].startBeforeReturn ?? program.stateTrace[pauseWeek]; state C5 for the break's own week; test: the same correction ten hours apart across Sunday/Monday gives the same plan.

newFindings.class: C1 same-day eligibility (QE-R7A-02 class) in the adaptation handlers
newFindings.mechanism: fatigueSessions (r6-composition.mjs:64), unavailableSessions (:72), conflictSessions (:96) and the move-slot filter (:52) add s.date > asOfLocal to aheadOf, so a session aheadOf calls ahead on the review's day (a PM session in the morning) is never adapted; the return path and every re-plan use aheadOf alone. Contract C1: 'Ahead has one definition for every handler (aheadOf)'.
newFindings.reproduction: qe-a1-P06-same-day-adaptations.mjs (A1 and FREEZE-2): runDays [1,3,6], strengthDays [0,3]; weeks 0-2 executed; week 3 Monday 06:00: UNAVAILABLE_DAY [that Monday] -> KEEP 'No planned session falls on the unavailable date' while d0PM strength 2x5 @82.5 stays; SYSTEMIC_FATIGUE -> Monday PM strength unchanged; EVENT_WEEK_CONFLICT [that Monday] in a race program week 12 -> kept; RETURN_AFTER_PAUSE at the same clock re-plans the Monday PM session to 1x5 @RIR4. qe-a1-P11: the mutant 'fatigue uses aheadOf alone' survives every test.
newFindings.requiredChange: Use aheadOf alone in these selectors (with each adaptation's own clock when re-applied); tests: a same-day PM session adapted by fatigue, by 'unavailable today' and by an event conflict today; an AM session after noon not adapted.

newFindings.class: I4 known-information preservation (QE-R7A-05 claim, same function)
newFindings.mechanism: mergeActual's filled (r6-provenance.mjs:41) fills a field only when null or undefined, while the ranking (exerciseFacts/kgOf) and every reader (strengthLogs) count a load with a missing or unreadable unit as unknown; when such an entry is chosen on a tie (equal known count, then the better declared source), the other report's readable load is never taken.
newFindings.reproduction: qe-a1-P07-merge-known-definitions.mjs: week-0 strength session; manual back-squat 3x(80 kg, 5 reps, no RIR); device (WEARABLE_FULL, same session) 3x(5 reps, RIR 3) with load {value:80} (no unit), 176 'LBS' or 176 'pounds'. Manual alone -> 80 kg. Both, either order -> load null, unitUnknown, question LOGGED_UNIT_OR_CONVENTION_UNKNOWN. Device load null (the author's case) -> 80 kg and loadTick 1. FREEZE-2 the same.
newFindings.requiredChange: One definition of known in the merge: fill from the other report's same set when the chosen set's load is unreadable (the predicate the ranking uses), keeping the raw value as provenance; tests with unitless and unknown-unit loads in both orders.

newFindings.mechanism: C3 treats the week as complete from ev.pending (date > asOfLocal), so a Sunday-morning re-plan gates the still-ahead Sunday session as NOT_REPORTED.
newFindings.reproduction: qe-a1-scratch-sundaymorning.mjs: SCHEDULE_CHANGE Sunday 07:00 gates LONG HOLD; the 21:00 weekly review gates it ADVANCE; no row effect observed.
newFindings.requiredChange: Read completeness with aheadOf (or document the reading); not required for READY.

newFindings.mechanism: A bodyweight-only equipment window's hinge substitute (glute-bridge, a catalogue ACCESSORY) lands in a race-window strength session when the race is moved; C7's phase dose (main lifts only) refuses the event change in either order.
newFindings.reproduction: qe-a1-P12-window-event-refusal.mjs: race program strengthDays [0,3], week 6 Monday 05:00 window BODYWEIGHT Wednesday-Thursday, 07:00 EVENT_DATE_CHANGE to Wednesday of week 7 -> UNSUPPORTED w6-str-d3:phaseDose:glute-bridge:accessory (A1 and FREEZE-2; also qe-a1-P09 O9, 6 occurrences of this one class).
newFindings.requiredChange: Fail-closed and no wrong plan; the substitution x race-window dose question goes to the SSCTR. Not required for READY.

newFindings.class: Dose effect reported to the SSCTR (not ruled here)
newFindings.mechanism: A systemic fatigue report that reduces the remaining sessions records SYSTEMIC_FATIGUE (no signal for the review); the same report with nothing left to reduce records SYSTEMIC_SIGNAL (the review holds).
newFindings.reproduction: qe-a1-P04 (forSSCTR): Thursday 21:00 report -> next week 7 exercises 3 -> 4 sets; Sunday 07:00 report -> next week holds at 3.
newFindings.requiredChange: SSCTR to rule whether a reducing systemic report also holds next week's steps.

Seeded random search, 5,000 sequences of 2-4 changes (same day, later days, across the week boundary with the weekly review), five programs (plain; three strength days; race week 6; race week 10 near the taper; PM runs with AM strength), 7 invariant oracles (qe-a1-P09): O1 0, O2 1 (= QE-R7A1-01), O3 0, O4 0, O6 0, O7 0, refusals 6 of one class (QE-R7A1-07), errors 0

Short return's easy slot re-applied after the eased slot is history with a later quality in the week: no generated program plans two quality runs a week (4 run-day sets x 3 goals, qe-a1-scratch-explore3); not reachable in these programs

evidenceAdequacy.tests: 495/495 (verifier). The R7-A.1 tests are metamorphic and property tests in the right direction. None covers the context validity of moved content, a change after the weekly review, a cross-week correction or unreadable loads in a merge.
evidenceAdequacy.grids: The order-equivalence relation on one clock is structural and caught 468 FREEZE-2 defects. It cannot see defects that hit both orders equally, that need a later step after the review, that cross the week boundary, or that compare a same-day adaptation against another handler. It uses one schedule shape per program, where no strength move is admissible.
evidenceAdequacy.mutation: 72/73 recorded; 4 entries reproduced independently (qe-a1-P11). The runs revert only the author's own fixes, so they cannot measure uncovered behaviour.
evidenceAdequacy.regression: Not rerun (prohibited); the verifier re-checks the recorded outputs and requires every named difference. Nothing I ran contradicts a named difference.
